title: Cartesian coordinate system and quadrants
prompt: The point P=(-5,7) is reflected in the y-axis. What is the new x-coordinate?
work: A reflection in the y-axis reverses the sign of x and leaves y unchanged.
restriction: Axis points have no quadrant.

title: Cartesian coordinate system and quadrants
prompt: Which quadrant contains a point with x<0 and y>0?
work: Quadrant II contains negative x-coordinates and positive y-coordinates.
restriction: Axis points have no quadrant.

title: Distance and midpoint in 2D
prompt: Find the distance between (1,2) and (4,6).
restriction: Use the same coordinate units on both axes.

title: Distance and midpoint in 2D
prompt: Which point is the midpoint of (2,4) and (8,10)?
work: Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately.
restriction: Use the same coordinate units on both axes.

title: Section formula and division of a segment
prompt: A point P divides A=(0,0) to B=(10,5) internally in ratio AP:PB=2:3. Find the x-coordinate of P.
restriction: The ratio must be directed correctly; external division uses a different formula.

title: Section formula and division of a segment
prompt: For AP:PB=1:1, where is P?
work: Equal internal ratios locate the midpoint.
restriction: The ratio must be directed correctly; external division uses a different formula.

title: Slope and inclination of a line
prompt: Find the slope through (2,1) and (8,7).
restriction: Vertical lines have undefined slope, not slope zero.

title: Slope and inclination of a line
prompt: What is the slope of x=4?
work: A vertical line has no finite run, so rise/run is undefined.
restriction: Vertical lines have undefined slope, not slope zero.

title: Parallel and perpendicular slopes
prompt: A line has slope −2. Find the slope of a perpendicular line.
restriction: Do not use negative-reciprocal arithmetic for a zero or undefined slope.

title: Parallel and perpendicular slopes
prompt: Which line is perpendicular to a horizontal line?
work: Horizontal and vertical directions are perpendicular.
restriction: Do not use negative-reciprocal arithmetic for a zero or undefined slope.

title: Point-slope and slope-intercept line equations
prompt: A line through (1,2) has slope 3. Find y when x=3.
restriction: Point–slope form with a finite m does not represent a vertical line.

title: Point-slope and slope-intercept line equations
prompt: Which form exposes the y-intercept b directly?
work: The constant b is the y-intercept in slope–intercept form.
restriction: Point–slope form with a finite m does not represent a vertical line.

title: Two-point and general line equations
prompt: For the line 2x+3y=12, find y when x=3.
restriction: Two identical points do not determine a unique line.

title: Two-point and general line equations
prompt: Which line equation represents a vertical line?
work: A vertical line fixes x, not y.
restriction: Two identical points do not determine a unique line.

title: Distance from a point to a line
prompt: Find the distance from (3,4) to the line 3x+4y−20=0.
restriction: The line coefficients A and B must not both be zero.

title: Distance from a point to a line
prompt: Why is there an absolute value in the numerator?
work: Signed substitution can be negative but geometric distance cannot.
restriction: The line coefficients A and B must not both be zero.

title: Intersections of two lines and angles between lines
prompt: Lines y=2x+1 and y=−x+7 intersect at what x-coordinate?
restriction: Parallel distinct lines do not have an intersection point.

title: Intersections of two lines and angles between lines
prompt: If two distinct lines have equal slopes, what follows?
work: Equal slopes with different intercepts describe parallel distinct lines.
restriction: Parallel distinct lines do not have an intersection point.

title: Locus equations and analytic proofs
prompt: A point is equally far from A=(0,0) and B=(6,0). What is its x-coordinate?
restriction: A locus equation must include all and only the points meeting the given condition.

title: Locus equations and analytic proofs
prompt: The points at a fixed distance r from a point form which locus?
work: The circle is defined by constant distance from its center.
restriction: A locus equation must include all and only the points meeting the given condition.

title: Circle equation: standard and general form
prompt: For x²+y²−4x+6y−12=0, find r².
restriction: A nonnegative radius squared is required for a real circle.

title: Circle equation: standard and general form
prompt: What is the center of (x−3)²+(y+2)²=16?
work: Compare with (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r²: the coordinate shifts are opposite to the signs displayed inside each square.
restriction: A nonnegative radius squared is required for a real circle.

title: Tangents and secants of coordinate circles
prompt: From P, the circle center is 13 units away and radius is 5. Find tangent length.
work: Use a right triangle joining external point P, center C, and tangency point T.
restriction: No real tangent segment from a point strictly inside the circle.

title: Tangents and secants of coordinate circles
prompt: A tangent line at T is perpendicular to what?
work: The radius to the tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent.
restriction: No real tangent segment from a point strictly inside the circle.

title: Parabola: vertex, focus, directrix, and equation
prompt: For y²=12x, find the x-coordinate of the focus.
restriction: The sign of p determines the opening direction.

title: Parabola: vertex, focus, directrix, and equation
prompt: For x²=−8y, which way does the parabola open?
work: x²=4py with p<0 opens in the negative y direction.
restriction: The sign of p determines the opening direction.

title: Ellipse: vertices, foci, axes, eccentricity
prompt: For an ellipse with a=5 and b=4, find c.
restriction: Require a≥b>0 and place foci on the major axis.

title: Ellipse: vertices, foci, axes, eccentricity
prompt: What range contains the eccentricity of a noncircular ellipse?
work: Ellipses satisfy 0≤e<1; a noncircular ellipse has 0<e<1.
restriction: Require a≥b>0 and place foci on the major axis.

title: Hyperbola: foci, axes, and asymptotes
prompt: For a hyperbola with a=3 and b=4, find c.
restriction: Hyperbola asymptote slopes depend on the transverse-axis orientation.

title: Hyperbola: foci, axes, and asymptotes
prompt: For x²/9−y²/16=1, which is the transverse axis?
work: The positive x² term indicates a horizontal transverse axis.
restriction: Hyperbola asymptote slopes depend on the transverse-axis orientation.

title: General second-degree equations and conic identification
prompt: For x²+4y²=16, compute Δ=B²−4AC.
restriction: The discriminant alone does not guarantee a nondegenerate real conic.

title: General second-degree equations and conic identification
prompt: If Δ>0, which generic conic type is indicated (assuming nondegenerate)?
work: Positive discriminant indicates hyperbolic type for a nondegenerate real conic.
restriction: The discriminant alone does not guarantee a nondegenerate real conic.

title: Translation and rotation of conic axes
prompt: The new origin is (3,1). A point is (8,6) in old coordinates. Find its new x-coordinate.
restriction: Do not confuse moving the axes with rotating a geometric figure.

title: Translation and rotation of conic axes
prompt: Which algebraic term can often be removed by a suitable rotation of axes?
work: Rotating principal axes diagonalizes the quadratic part and can eliminate xy.
restriction: Do not confuse moving the axes with rotating a geometric figure.

title: Polar coordinates and conversions
prompt: For polar coordinates (r,θ)=(10,30°), find x to four decimals.
restriction: Polar representations are not unique and negative radii require care.

title: Polar coordinates and conversions
prompt: Which polar representation denotes the origin?
work: At r=0, angle does not affect position.
restriction: Polar representations are not unique and negative radii require care.

title: Parametric curves and parametric equations
prompt: A curve has x=2+3t, y=1−t. What is x at t=4?
restriction: Different parameter intervals can trace different portions or orientations of the same curve.

title: Parametric curves and parametric equations
prompt: What does the parameter t describe?
options: Always the distance from the origin
A common variable controlling the coordinates
Always the angle with the x-axis
work: A parameter determines the position on the curve through coordinate functions.
restriction: Different parameter intervals can trace different portions or orientations of the same curve.

title: Geometric vectors and vector operations
prompt: Let u=(3,4), v=(1,−4). Find the x-component of u+v.
restriction: A vector is not just a point; displacement is independent of the choice of origin.

title: Geometric vectors and vector operations
prompt: What is the magnitude of vector (3,4)?
restriction: A vector is not just a point; displacement is independent of the choice of origin.

title: Dot product, cross product, and direction cosines
restriction: Dot and cross products are different operations; a zero dot product means orthogonal for nonzero vectors.

title: Dot product, cross product, and direction cosines
prompt: If two nonzero vectors have zero dot product, they are:
restriction: Dot and cross products are different operations; a zero dot product means orthogonal for nonzero vectors.

title: 3D Cartesian distance and midpoint
prompt: Find the 3D distance between (1,2,3) and (4,6,15).
restriction: Coordinates must be measured in consistent units.

title: 3D Cartesian distance and midpoint
prompt: The midpoint z-coordinate for z₁=2 and z₂=8 is:
restriction: Coordinates must be measured in consistent units.

title: Lines in space and parametric line equations
prompt: For x=1+2t, y=3−t, z=4+t, find x when t=3.
restriction: At least one direction component must be nonzero.

title: Lines in space and parametric line equations
prompt: What fixes the direction of a parametric line in 3D?
work: A nonzero vector gives the line direction.
restriction: At least one direction component must be nonzero.

title: Planes in three-space and normal vectors
prompt: For 2x+3y+6z=12, find z when x=0 and y=0.
restriction: A,B,C must not all vanish.

title: Planes in three-space and normal vectors
prompt: Which vector is normal to 2x+3y+6z=12?
work: Coefficients of x,y,z form a normal vector.
restriction: A,B,C must not all vanish.

title: Equation of a sphere in three-space
prompt: For (x−1)²+(y+2)²+(z−3)²=49, find r.
restriction: A negative right-hand side gives no real sphere.

title: Equation of a sphere in three-space
prompt: What is the center of (x+2)²+y²+(z−5)²=9?
work: The signs inside the shifted squares reverse when reading the center.
restriction: A negative right-hand side gives no real sphere.

title: Quadric surfaces: ellipsoids, paraboloids, hyperboloids
prompt: For x²/9+y²/16+z²/25=1, find the longest semiaxis.
restriction: A quadratic form can represent a degenerate or imaginary surface for some constants.

title: Quadric surfaces: ellipsoids, paraboloids, hyperboloids
prompt: Which equation describes an elliptic paraboloid opening upward?
work: The cross-section z=x²+y² is nonnegative and increases away from the origin.
restriction: A quadratic form can represent a degenerate or imaginary surface for some constants.

title: Analytic area and coordinate-based geometry proofs
prompt: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,0),(6,0),(0,4).
work: The shoelace determinant gives the same result: 12 square units.
restriction: The listed vertices must follow the polygon boundary without self-crossing.

title: Analytic area and coordinate-based geometry proofs
prompt: Why take the absolute value in the shoelace formula?
options: Negative area is a valid physical area
Vertex order can reverse the sign
work: Reversing vertex orientation negates signed area, not physical area.
restriction: The listed vertices must follow the polygon boundary without self-crossing.
